short: STFM and the convolutional encoder-decoder (M06) are standard: layout-keeping reduction predates it, baselines are weakened; LRW SOTA claim fails; LM use never stated (M07).
position: The paper [@zhang2019convseq2seq] changes M06 twice, both standard: STFM replaces global average pooling, and a convolutional encoder-decoder with width-restricted self-attention replaces the Transformer. Keeping the layout was not new: 7 of 13 prior lip readers stating their reduction use a fully connected layer over the map, one with a direct ablation [@stafylakis2018pushing] (Appendix); STFM is tested only against average pooling. Its encoder-decoder gains come against baselines the authors call inconsistent with the originals (§4.2); with about half the training video (863 against 1,637.4, Table 4; inference), the final 51.7% and 60.1% WER on LRS2 and LRS3 come within 1.9 and 0.2 points of TM-seq2seq without an LM [@afouras2018deep], supporting "comparable" (§4.3), not a better sequence model. The state-of-the-art claim (§5) holds on GRID, fails on LRW against an earlier 15.67% error [@stafylakis2018pushing], and the paper's own LM condition is unstated (§3.5, M07).
